_comment: Tier-2 for NGSolve phase_field#0: Allen-Cahn does not conserve mass, the mixed H1xH1 Cahn-Hilliard form does. Verified on NGSolve 6.2.2604, unit_square maxh=0.06 (ne=634, P1 ndof=352), eps=0.06, droplet radius 0.3, M=20, dt=2e-4, 60 steps (2026-08-06): the shipped semi-implicit Allen-Cahn scheme drifts by -2.755e-02 relative and monotonically, while the same mesh/eps/M/dt under a stabilised semi-implicit Cahn-Hilliard on ProductSpace(H1,H1) drifts by -3.516e-16. Both fields stay inside [0,1] to a few percent, so the drift is genuine curvature-driven shrinkage rather than an instability. MUTATION CONTROL (re-runnable): T2_MUTATE=1 solves the run whose mass drift is measured with the documented fix -- the mass-conserving mixed (c, mu) Cahn-Hilliard form (cahn_hilliard()) on the same mesh, eps, M and dt -- instead of the semi-implicit Allen-Cahn scheme. Re-verified by execution 2026-08-06 on NGSolve 6.2.2604: the unmutated run matches all 9 expect_in_output strings; T2_MUTATE=1 removes 'ac_mass_drift_gt_1pct=True', 'ac_mass_monotone_decreasing=True' and 'ch_conserves_better_than_ac_by_gt_1e10=True' so the fixture goes red.
